meaningMnemonic: If you want to wear a top hat you also have to wear a suit to go with it. You can't just wear a top hat, that just doesn't look right. When you think top hat, think about what you also need with it. Hints Picture all the things you also need. A suit, a tie, a monocle, some shiny shoes. There's also ... something... else. What is it?
readingMnemonic: You have a top hat and all the clothes that go with it but you also need a nice ca r ( か ) too! You can't just get all dressed up and then have no way to get anywhere to show it off. Hints Think about all the things you also need when you wear a top hat. The car is probably the most important addition. Otherwise no one can see the top hat in the first place!

meaningMnemonic: When the sun comes up the spikes of geoduck s appear . Hints The spikes don't just come out of the geoduck, they literally appear out of thin air. They didn't even exist before the sun touched them.
readingMnemonic: You watch these spikes appear and suddenly Ken ( けん )the samurai also appears next to you. "I DID IT!" he shouts, "I've learned how to appear out of thin air!" Hints "Thank you sweet geoduck, you have taught me the way of appearing with your spikes."

meaningMnemonic: What does a tree make that you'd want to put in your mouth ? An apricot ! Apricots are also about the size of an open mouth, so they kind of look like mouths hanging down under the trees. You can bite them right off the tree with your own mouth! Hints Picture the mouth sized apricots hanging down off the tree. Imagine using your own mouth to bite them down. Just don't swallow the pit!
readingMnemonic: After you put the apricot in your mouth you realize that this tastes really familiar, but not pleasant. It tastes just like the an chovies ( あん ) from the zoo ( ず ) smell. How did that happen? You don't like apricots anymore. Hints Imagine trying to eat the bite sized apricot and spitting it out after the taste of anchovies from the zoo fill you up.

meaningMnemonic: Dry an already dry tree to create a bookmark . The more you dry the tree, the flatter it becomes, making it the perfect way to mark your spot in a book without needing to fold a page or write on it. Hints To be fair, books are just dry trees in a way, but bookmarks are actually dry, dry trees that have flattened out and turned into chunks.
readingMnemonic: What are you bookmarking anyway? Look down and see yourself putting one of the tree bookmark s on a page in your notebook that says " She owe s me ree ds ( しおり )." Oh yeah, you had to make this bookmark in the first place because your friend took your reed bookmarks and didn't give them back. Hints What does she owe you? Open the page to your bookmark and see she owes reeds!

meaningMnemonic: You see a bunch of tree s lined up outside of the gate to the east and realize they look like perfect column s. It seems like a building or a castle should be resting above them. Hints Picture these column trees outside the gate to the east. You end up drawing them in the columns of your graph paper because they fit so well.
readingMnemonic: Out of the tree column s bursts professional wrestler Ran dy ( らん ) Savage! "Oooh I'm talking about columns that I like mmmm oh yeaah. The Macho Man loves columns MMm OOHH YEAAH~!" Hints Now draw Randy Savage in the columns on your graph paper. He just seems to fit there now.

meaningMnemonic: Who goes into their yurt to boil things? The common people! All sorts of people do it, it's really common. You don't boil things outside, do you? Hints Wait, you're telling me you didn't know it's common to boil things in yurts? Excuse me?
readingMnemonic: Here, the common people all do this, so just let me show ( しょ ) you how. First you go into your yurt, and… Hey, pay attention and watch what I'm showing you! Hints Okay, now that I've shown you what to do, you can fit in with the common people here.

meaningMnemonic: Your forehead is the origin for the measurement for your crown ! If you measure somewhere else on your head for a crown it won't fit. Hints Imagine someone putting a tape measure around your forehead and taking careful measurements for your crown. They better not mess up, or you'll have them put to death!
readingMnemonic: You want your crown to be just like Genghis Khan 's ( かん ), which was more of a cap. He's your hero though, because he ruled over the most people, so you want yours to match his measurements. Hints Why don't you go look up what Genghis Khan's crown/cap looked like. Then try to imagine how it would look atop your head.

meaningMnemonic: If you announce that alcohol is illegal you're just being cruel . Honestly, saying no one can have any alcohol at all is totally unjust . They tried that in the 1920s and it didn't work then either, so cut it out! Let people drink what they want to drink! Hints Imagine if your country's leader announced that there would be no more alcohol. People would be in the streets in seconds calling them cruel and unjust!
readingMnemonic: After this cruel announcement is made everyone will turn to the next best thing after alcohol. Coke ( こく )! It's not a replacement, but if this unjust law won't change, then coke sales are going to go through the roof. Hints Imagine drinking coke while complaining how unjust it is that you can't add rum to it.

meaningMnemonic: The surplus stool , please describe it. Hints You have a surplus (extra) stool, and someone wants it. But, they need to know more about it, so you describe it in great detail. Imagine yourself doing just that. Every screw and nubbin is described.
readingMnemonic: You describe the features of the stool to Jo -Anne ( じょ ). Hints Jo-Anne is really excited about this stool. It's the perfect height for her (remember, she's on the shorter side to distinguish じょ from じょう ). She pays attention to you describing the stool while sitting on it and spinning around. Have her ask for you to describe it more.

meaningMnemonic: Jump on a scooter to excuse yourself from answering a question and you've successfully deviate d from that nosey person's plan! You've also been able to elude them pretty well. Hints Imagine excusing yourself by scooting away on a scooter. If they want to get your answer, they'll have to chase you.
readingMnemonic: You deviate from the plan a little too well, and as you're scooting, what you've done eats ( いつ ) away at you. You feel guilty for eluding them... Hints Welp, it's too late to turn back now. You've already deviated pretty far, and you're not even sure where you are now. You were too busy trying to elude that person that you didn't look where your scooter was taking you.

meaningMnemonic: You use thread and writing to sew our family crest . You've been sewing your family crest since you were a kid, you could do it today with your eyes closed. Hints Imagine the thread slowly forming the writing that makes up your family crest. You're making a scarf with your crest on it. It's like a wizarding school house symbol.
readingMnemonic: Your family crest is of a mon ster! ( もん ) And the writing says "Our Family Monster." Hints What kind of monster is on your family crest? Picture it in your mind right now. Now tweet to us @wanikaniapp because I really want to know what you came up with!!

meaningMnemonic: You see a building with a lip ring and it's just so cute you have to flatter it. "That lip ring looks wonderful on you, Building さん ," you say. Hints Flattering buildings is just as nice as flattering people, as long as they're okay with it.
readingMnemonic: The building is flatter ed and you hear it shout, " Ah ( あ )!" and blush. The entire building turns red. Hints The "ah" the building made was actually quite loud, and since you've never heard a building speak before, it scared you pretty bad. But at least you know the building was flattered by your compliment (I think.)

meaningMnemonic: If you give Splinter your heart you'll feel pretty foolish afterwards. His heart belongs to the art of ninjutsu! Hints You were foolish to give your heart away to Splinter. He didn't want it. Also he's a rat, what's wrong with you?
readingMnemonic: Splinter tells you to your face how foolish you are and you feel your heart turn to goo ( ぐ ). Now you can't even give it to someone else. No one wants goo. Hints What will you do with your foolish goo heart now?

meaningMnemonic: A triceratops with a mustache will go on talking forever. Every time you think he's done he says, " Furthermore ..." and keeps going. Something about a mustache on a dinosaur makes him kind of a jerk, but he's held in such high esteem that no one ever interrupts him. Hints Imagine this mustachioed triceratops. He probably has a monocle and a fedora too. Every time you think you can talk or leave he says, "Furthermore" again. Come on guy, how much do you have to say?
readingMnemonic: Why don't you just interrupt this mustache triceratops while he's saying furthermore ? Because he's the Shou gun's ( しょう ) pet. If you interrupt him you'll probably be put to death or something. Just let him keep going and hope he runs out of furthermores to talk about. Hints "Furthermore!" the mustachioed triceratops points at the Shougun, "He is the best Shougun we'll ever have. And he'll let me talk forever OH OH OH!"

meaningMnemonic: A mouth with a sword is threatening to cut off your fingers because they've kidnap ped you! You can't see anything about them, since they're all covered up. All you see is their angry mouth and the sword they keep putting near your fingers. Hints Imagine you've been kidnapped. And the person who kidnapped you is going to cut off some of your fingers and mail them to your parents if they don't pay the ransom soon enough. You don't want your fingers to be cut off with a sword! Help!
readingMnemonic: You've been kidnap ped and your kidnapper has asked for one thing in exchange for your safe return: a kay ak ( かい ). Kayaks are expensive. And it's way easier for this dude to kidnap you and demand your family buy one and give it to them than for them to work for one. Hints If your parents don't send in the kayak to your kidnapper soon, you're gonna lose some fingers. Come on guys, just get the kayak already!!!

meaningMnemonic: The leader who usually hits you with a stick in winter finds it in his heart to give you some leisure time. Hints You fall to your knees, "Oh thank you for not hitting me with your stick and letting me relax!" You haven't had a moment of leisure in ages!
readingMnemonic: You're just about to start your leisure time when a group of you ths ( ゆう ) appears with their own sticks. You look back for the leader, and he's wearing a bathrobe, sunglasses, and is drinking some hot cocoa. Wait... this is leisure time for... HIM?! OH NO! Hints As the leader leisurely watches, the youths smack you with their sticks. What a cruel world! "Enjoy your leisure time," the leader yells over, "the youths hit much softer than I do. Have fun!"

meaningMnemonic: You feel heavy because power boil s within you. This is a sign of your merit . Individuals with great merit tend to see power not as a blessing, but as a heavy burden. Hints Feel the power boiling inside you. Now feel the heavy responsibility to use that power for meritorious deeds.
readingMnemonic: Your merit comes from your mastery of kun g fu ( くん ). You only use your kung fu skills to perform merit-worthy deeds, like defending the weak and vulnerable. Hints Imagine using your kung fu abilities to do something really meritorious, like saving an old lady from a mugger or running up the trunk of a tall tree, wuxia-style, to rescue someone's cat.

meaningMnemonic: A coat rack will turn into a bundle of sticks if you neglect it. When you neglect a coat rack, the weight from the coats will pull all of the arms off, leaving it as a sparse stick. Hints Picture this sparse, neglected coat rack. All of its arms and the coats that were on it have fallen off and are in a big pile on the ground.
readingMnemonic: You go up to the neglect ed coat rack and try to make things right by cleaning it with so ap ( そ ). But no matter how much you scrub, it won't get clean, the arms won't go back on. Hints If you neglect something for too long, not even a good soap scrub will bring it back. That goes for humans too. Take care of yourselves. Use soap.

meaningMnemonic: Whatever you say through a satellite turns into Noh chanting . It gets all drawn out and distorted from going through the satellite, which makes it SOUND like Noh chanting at least. Hints Say whatever you want and send it up to the satellite. Now imagine listening to it when it comes back and hearing beautiful, deep Noh chanting back!
readingMnemonic: While you're fake Noh chanting you have to pause every few minutes to take a bite of yo gurt ( よう ). Yogurt is good for the throat! At least you think it is. It's not like you're actually chanting, the satellite is doing all the real work. Hints Watch closely the next time you go to a Noh play. See the man Noh chanting? Watch close enough and you'll see him eat a scoop of yogurt every once in a while.

meaningMnemonic: A drunkard gets his hands on a plow and starts planting right away. Drunk people are surprisingly good at planting, especially when they have machines to help them do it. Hints Picture a drunk guy laughing and plowing a field and planting seeds. He wouldn't do this if he was sober, but drunk people can't help themselves.
readingMnemonic: He keeps planting and planting... a little too much. You walk over and realize this drunkard isn't just any guy... he's YOUR CY BORG ( さい )! Hints Oh my sweet cyborg child! Is this what they've done with you? You're just a drunkard who's only good for planting? Nooooooo!!

meaningMnemonic: Whenever you set foot in a bar , there's always something new to practice . If you usually drink a lot, you might want to practice moderation for example. Or perhaps you simply want to brush up on your social skills. Either way, plenty of opportunities for practice. Hints Are you the kind to practice flirting with the bartender, or are you more the kind to engage in a bit of small talk with the other patrons? Maybe you're just trying to practice patience while the bartender is talking instead of getting your order ready.
readingMnemonic: This type of practice is especially hard for you because you're a cen taur ( せん ). You only have hooves for feet, and balancing on a bar is going to be a huge hurdle. But your teacher promised if you practiced enough you could make it, and here you are! With your hoofed foot on the bar! Hints Picture your centaur foot on the bar as you practice to become a gymnast. It's going to take years and years of this kind of practice, but you're sure you'll make it all the way up there some day! Never give up!

meaningMnemonic: The Mouth King , who is just one big mouth, has one skill, and that is to present . That big mouth is always presenting something. Hints Imagine the Mouth King giving a presentation about the importance of mouths. His subjects all flatter him by saying, "Please, please, present to us about mouths again! We truuuuuuly love it!"
readingMnemonic: "I will present to you a presentation about mouths, but I require energy. Please fill my giant mouth body with delicious ta ter ( てい ) tots. Hints You pour a bucket of tater tots into his mouth body and he continues his presentation about mouths. "You see, mouths are just orifices..."

meaningMnemonic: Your leader managed to find the right direction home using marks in the dirt in the middle of winter . This makes you so proud ! You're proud because this resourceful leader is YOUR resourceful leader. Hints Imagine how proud you and your whole country feel as your leader comes trudging in through the snow. He made it home. You're (sniff) so (sob) proud!
readingMnemonic: This leader you're so proud of is none other than Grandpa ごう いち . He's been getting a bit slow over the years, and you really didn't think he'd make it back. But, by gum, he did it. Hints Let's be honest here, Grandpa ごういち isn't getting any younger. You really should be proud of him for surviving this long at all.

meaningMnemonic: A sick ness that hits you like an arrow will do its gross work rapidly . It's not a good thing, you're gonna get really sick really fast. Hints Picture this rapid sickness spreading through your body like a cartoon arrow ricocheting through your body. Yuck!
readingMnemonic: This rapid sickness makes your head pound like there's a shih tzu ( しつ ) yapping and barking nonstop. And it's making you sh*t a lot. Hints Imagine getting sick this rapidly. All of a sudden, there's a shih tzu barking in your head, it hurts! And... oh no, where's the toilet?!

meaningMnemonic: You took someone's alcohol and drop drop drop 'd it all into the river . Now you have to repay them. Alcohol costs a lot of money, you know. Hints Picture yourself dropping the alcohol, drop by drop, into the river. Uh oh, the person just caught up to you, so you better repay them.
readingMnemonic: In order to repay them for the alcohol you wasted, you offer to give them your shoe s ( しゅう ). They don't want your shoes though, so you have to bring them to a store and watch them try on a bunch of different pairs so you can repay them that way. Hints Imagine waiting as this person tries on like twenty different pairs of shoes. They're getting them for free! Why do they have to be picky?! Just let me repay you already!

meaningMnemonic: What kind of flowers grow in the west ? Rose madder flowers, of course. Don't know what those are? That's okay. Just know their roots are used to make dyes of a deep red color. Red like the rose in their name, but madder, wilder, deeper… And they grow in the west so they can take in those deep red colors of the setting sun. Hints Picture yourself sitting in the west as the red sun sets, smashing those little rose madder roots into a paste to make your deep red dyes. Your fingers turn red from the rose madder too.
readingMnemonic: As you smash the roots of the rose madder and stain your fingers a deep red , a little girl comes up to you and points. She says, " 赤ね ( あかね )?" (That's red, right?) You look down at the rose madder roots and your fingers, and nod. She's right, it is red. Deep red. Hints Hear the little girl say あかね while pointing at the rose madder and your deep red fingers. She's right. And the way she says it is so darn cute.

meaningMnemonic: You see a mouth coming out of the top of a tree so you go into shock . Your brain just can't comprehend what's in front of you. Hints A tree... with... a... mouth? No, it can't be... I... a-. Your face warps into a permanent state of shock.
readingMnemonic: The shock you've suffered results in you needing to stay ho me ( ほう ) from now on. You don't get to travel, explore, or even get groceries. You're homebound from now on, buddy. Hints I'd be shocked if you ever left your home again, honestly. But hey, there's always anime.

meaningMnemonic: You cover the Mona Lisa in gold and attach it to a stick to turn it into a sickle ! It's really big and bulky, but when you swing it fast enough your new sickle cuts lots of wheat! Just don't tell anyone what you did with the famous Mona Lisa painting and you should be able to get away with this! Hints Imagine wielding your gold Mona Lisa sickle. It's sooo heavy, but it's really shiny and it cuts grass and wheat pretty well!
readingMnemonic: Now that you've turned the Mona Lisa into a sickle , you have to change the little description under its name in the Louvre. You draw a giant comma ( かま ) next to "Mona Lisa" and write "THE SICKLE." Then you shove it back on the wall as best you can. Hints Hear all the guests say, "Mona Lisa... comma the sickle? WHAT'S HAPPENED HERE?!" As panic ensues. You like your addition and you're very proud.

meaningMnemonic: Wolverine puts a stick between his legs and straight into some rice , all while wearing a solemn expression on his face. He's probably remembering his dad who died from getting his legs stuck in rice. Just leave the poor solemn creature alone. Hints Putting a stick in some rice is a ritual that Wolverine practices to mark solemn occasions. Shh, listen up! He's probably about to say something solemn and important about his dad.
readingMnemonic: When you first saw how solemn Wolverine was after his dad died, it really shook ( しゅく ) you. Now you're used to always seeing him emotionally cold and distant. It might be time to shake that solemnity out of him though. Hints Do you think you could shake the solemnness out of someone? Imagine being shooketh so hard, you stop feeling solemn. Wouldn't that be great?

meaningMnemonic: When you leave flowers on a tombstone they look good at first, but after a few days or some harsh weather, there's nothing left but stem s. That's why you have to replace flowers on tombstones all the time. If you don't it will look like you only left the stems there, and that's pretty disrespectful. Hints Imagine being in a graveyard looking at all the tombstones and seeing nothing but stems on all of them. All the pretty flowery parts have died and blown away.
readingMnemonic: You have an idea that can make these tombstones look better than just having leftover stem s all over them. You brought cookie s ( くき )! Cookies don't fall apart in the wind, and everyone loves cookies, alive or dead. You replace the stems with the cookies and everything looks a lot nicer. Hints Look at all the cookie covered tombstones. Now your bag is full of stems, but you can use them to make more cookies to bring back next time. Don't worry, nobody eats them. Stem cookies are probably poisonous.

meaningMnemonic: You're sick because you put an arrow in your mouth and tried to eat it. To be honest, that's just really stupid . You have to be stupid to try to eat an arrow. You deserve to be sick. Hints How stupid do you have to be to put arrows into your mouth until it makes you sick? Pretty darn stupid, it seems.
readingMnemonic: The only way to cure this serious case of stupid is to make you eat chee se ( ち ). Not only will it fix your sick stomach by cushioning all the arrows that you shoved in your stupid mouth, but it should send smart cheese waves to your brain and cure you of that stupid all together. Hints Imagine if everyone knew that cheese cures the stupid out of people. Then maybe we would have more cheese and less stupid in the world!

meaningMnemonic: After your wedding you have a baby and it uses its mouth to suckle from your post-wedding boobs. Yes, babies nurse from breasts. Get over it, kids. Hints You waited until your wedding to have your baby and all it seems to do with its mouth is suckle. It doesn't cry, which is nice, but it doesn't laugh or talk either.
readingMnemonic: The baby wants to nurse all day and the only thing you can seem to do at the same time is hoe ( ほ ) your garden. You hold the baby to your breast with one arm and hoe little rows with the other. It's actually a great workout and a nice way to spend time! Hints This hoe has really helped you get through nursing. You think you'll keep this up even after your baby is weaned! Hoeing the garden is your new favorite hobby!

meaningMnemonic: Clearing his flowers of icicle s, the samurai returns home to his villa . Hints Picture the samurai's villa. It's in the countryside and covered in flowers and icicles. Even though it's spring, it's still cold, so all the new flowers are very cold.
readingMnemonic: Once the samurai enters the villa , he lets his soul ( そう ) go. He's been fighting for long enough and this villa was always where he wanted to go. Hints Picture the samurai sitting in a chair in his beautiful villa and breathing his last breath. His soul slowly floats up and out of his still body and dances around the villa, free.

meaningMnemonic: If you travel to the fish capital , you'll find the leader of all fish, the mighty whale ! Okay, so a whale isn't technically a fish, but that's why it makes such a good leader. You can usually only find whales hanging around near the capital because they really enjoy ruling over all the other fish. They are the biggest, after all. Hints Picture the underwater fish capital. Statues of whales line the fishy streets, and all of the fish bow down to the whale ruler's giant body.
readingMnemonic: The whale who resides over the capital just happens to be gay ( げい ). You only know this because his husband is a man whale too. Actually, now that you think about it, all the whales you've ever met have been gay. Hints Picture the gay whale ruler holding whale hands... fins? with his whale husband. They're so cute.

meaningMnemonic: At noon you stop to buy stamp s because that's the only time they're being sold at wholesale price. Everyone's so busy eating and working and being at school, that they miss this awesome deal, but not you. Everyday at noon you stock up on wholesale stamps. Do you send a lot of mail? No, you probably just collect them. But they were cheap, so who cares! Hints Imagine yourself stopping at the empty bank at noon, grabbing a handful of wholesale stamps. So many stamps. So few extra charges.
readingMnemonic: Oh, one more thing. Going at noon isn't enough, you have to say the password to get them at wholesale price too. The password is " Oh Roshi " ( おろし ). Okay, so maybe that's just the name of the guy there, but it always works when I want to get stamps wholesale so you should do it too! Hints "Oh Roshi" you say carefully as you hand your stamps over at noon. The guy raises an eyebrow at you, but gives you them wholesale! It worked!

Fun fact: the word originally means "to return from 黄泉 ( よみ )," the land of the dead in Japanese mythology. readingMnemonic: The person you most want to be resurrected is the 読み -guy ( よみがえ ) — the guy who teaches you the readings of difficult kanji. He died from overwork after you asked him too many kanji readings, so you really want him to come back to life and help you study some more. Alternatively, you can remember this as 黄泉 ( よみ ) + 帰る : coming home from the land of the dead. Just don't forget the rendaku on 帰る !

meaningMnemonic: 噴 means eruption , and 出す can mean "to let out," right? Well if you let out an eruption, it's probably going to cause something to burst out . You know, like lava out of a volcano. Or maybe it's going to to spout out , like a geyser out of the earth. This may remind you of another word you've learned: 吹き出す . They're very similar and often interchangeable, but in general 噴き出す is used for things that spout out with even more power and intensity. Along those lines, it can also be used figuratively, like when pent-up emotions burst out suddenly.
readingMnemonic: Remember how you learned the word 吹き出す ? Well, this is read the exact same way and means almost the exact same thing. If you know one reading, you know both!

meaningMnemonic: This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means lazy or neglect , and this verb means basically the same thing — to slack off , to be lazy , or to neglect . 怠ける is a word you use to describe someone who skips study time, avoids chores, or isn't trying very hard at something — even though they should be. It can sound critical, but it isn't nearly as heavy as words like 怠慢 or 怠惰 , and it can even be used in a light or joking way sometimes.
